listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, November 10. Our lead story is from the world of Claude. Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 yesterday. Simon Willison reports that Fable 5.2 is currently ranked first on Artificial Analysis. Anthropic says the model solved two open problems in the physics of black holes. Willison has updated his llm-anthropic tool for the new models. The Claude platform notes say Fable 5.2 is built for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work. Mythos 5.2 offers the same capabilities, but only to organizations verified through Anthropic's programs. A fast mode for Fable 5.2 on the Claude API offers up to two and a half times higher output speed. Now the rest of the front page. In Abu Dhabi, Kyiv, Washington and Moscow have sent delegations to the first three-way talks since February. US officials cite some flexibility on the warring sides. In Washington, Thomas Massie filed articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. They cite the war against Iran and the War Powers Resolution. In football, the NFL reinstated 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk. San Francisco has a two-game roster exemption for him. Now the sections. In tech, Meta AI launched a small, efficient model called Muse Ember, and Anthropic's Agent Skills repository is trending on GitHub. In politics, California voters defeated a one-time five percent billionaire tax. The Lever reports on a coming Democratic debate over taxing the rich. Drop Site covers flooding in Gaza and Saudi strikes in Yemen. In world news, Trump says more US attacks on Iran are highly unlikely. France says Iranian military hackers took over refrigeration controllers at about seven hundred retail sites. In sports, Kevin Durant and Alperen Sengun led the Rockets past the Nuggets, one hundred ten to one hundred. Christian McCaffrey broke an NFL record in the 49ers' win over the Raiders. In Atlanta, a Beltline project has started delivering the first of three hundred twenty-five more residences. The College Football Playoff will grow to twenty-four teams, which ends the SEC title game played in Atlanta. In architecture, Trimble is adding AI agents to its Connect platform. G2 Digital launched a quad-GPU server as an alternative to cloud AI. In science, fossil fuel emissions are down in 2026, probably because of high gas prices from the Iran war. Arctic ice cores also trace heavy metals to old mining in Montana. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: llm-anthropic 0.31
lead.note: Anthropic released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 today, according to Simon Willison's note on the llm-anthropic 0.31 release. He reports that Fable 5.2 is currently ranked first on Artificial Analysis. Anthropic says the model solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, and Willison remarks that its internal benchmarks have clearly become more ambitious. For a reader who builds personal tools with Claude, the practical point is that the plugin release notes say the new models have been added. The item is a short release note, so it offers little beyond the ranking and Anthropic's claim. Both are claims to weigh, not settled facts. Even so, it is the most direct Claude news today and a prompt to read the platform notes on what the new models are built for.
